purpose: Ross Cameron style gap-and-go: does a gapping small-cap that breaks its first 5-minute high in the first hour have a net edge? Same rule as the live shadow signal cameron_gap.
data: Local 5-minute SIP candles (regular hours) and daily bars of the 400-stock sample S of research/round2 (data/m5, data/daily_S.json). Development period only; the locked period is not downloaded unless the hypothesis passes.
limits: No premarket data (gap = first 5-minute open vs previous daily close), no float, no news filter. The sample is 400 random stocks, so the number of gappers per day is small.

signal.gap: open of the first 5-minute candle / previous daily close - 1 >= +5%
signal.price: close of the signal candle between 2 and 20 USD
signal.relativeVolume: cumulative volume since the open / (mean daily volume of the previous 20 sessions x elapsed minutes / 390) >= 2
signal.trigger: first closed 5-minute candle (candle index 1..11, i.e. 10 to 60 minutes after the open) whose close is above the high of the first candle; no earlier candle closed above it
signal.stop: low of the first candle; skipped when the stop is more than 8% below the signal close
signal.entry: open of the candle after the signal candle
signal.exit: stop, target, or the last candle's close (stop wins when one candle touches both; a candle opening beyond the level exits at its open)

control: same rule but with an absolute gap below 1% (no gap), same price and relative-volume filters

statistic.primary: mean net R of the gap group, per-date means, one-sided date-block bootstrap p (blocks of 20 dates, 2000 resamples) for mean <= 0
statistic.secondary: gap group minus control, date-matched, same bootstrap

passRule: primary p < 0.05 AND mean net R > 0 AND at least 100 trades AND at least 2 of 3 calendar years with positive mean net R AND excess over control > 0
report: max drawdown of cumulative per-date mean R
concentration in the best 5% of dates
share of trades stopped on the entry candle
noTuning: Thresholds are fixed now and not varied after the results.
